hooks.text: No human-made object had ever crossed the asteroid belt or reached Jupiter.
Pioneer 10 was the first spacecraft to reach our solar system's escape velocity.
One nuclear probe was the first to travel past the asteroid belt.

title: Pioneer 10: The First Scout to Jupiter
description: In 1972, Pioneer 10 became the first spacecraft to navigate the asteroid belt and reach Jupiter. Carrying humanity's golden greeting card, it blazed a trail into interstellar space.

beats.text: No human-made object had ever crossed the asteroid belt or reached Jupiter.
beats.visual: NASA artist concept of Pioneer 10 approaching Jupiter, 1972

beats.text: In 1972, Pioneer 10 launched aboard an Atlas-Centaur rocket, powered entirely by nuclear generators.
beats.visual: photograph of Pioneer 10 launching on Atlas-Centaur rocket, March 1972

beats.text: It safely navigated the asteroid belt and flew within 82,000 miles of Jupiter in 1973.
beats.visual: Pioneer 10 photograph of Jupiter and the Great Red Spot, 1973

beats.text: Intense Jovian radiation triggered false commands in the probe, yet it returned over 500 images.
beats.visual: Pioneer 10 image showing radiation noise during Jupiter flyby, 1973

beats.text: Its hull carried a gold plaque designed by Carl Sagan, depicting two humans and 14 pulsars.
beats.visual: official NASA photograph of the Pioneer 10 gold-anodized plaque, 1972

beats.text: In 1983, it passed Neptune's orbit, but navigators soon noticed a tiny, unexplained drift in its signal.
beats.visual: NASA diagram showing Pioneer 10 trajectory past Neptune into deep space

beats.text: This famous Pioneer Anomaly was eventually solved: the recoil of uneven heat radiation was gently tugging it.
beats.visual: technical diagram of thermal recoil radiation causing the Pioneer Anomaly, 2012

beats.text: Silent since 2003, the spacecraft drifts toward the star Aldebaran after proving what deep-space probes could survive.
beats.visual: telescope image of the red giant star Aldebaran in constellation Taurus

better_than_last: Replaced technical jargon with direct physical action in the hook and structured the anomaly reveal as an escalating mystery to prevent midpoint drop-off.
